# Jubilees Chapter 6 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Noah's Offerings; Covenant; Blood Prohibition; 364-Day Calendar

---

**6:1** And on the new moon of the third month he went out of the ark, and he built an altar on that mountain, and he called on the name of the LORD and said: "You, the LORD God of our ancestors, do not let your face fall away from the children of Noah and from the seed of Shem; and let not Japheth go far from you; and may God dwell in the dwelling-places of Shem, and let Canaan be his servant, and let him be a servant of his brothers."

**6:2** And he made on that day a burnt-offering to the LORD, from all of the beasts and from all of the clean birds; a he-goat as a sin offering, and a calf and a sheep, and a dove and a turtle-dove for burnt-offerings, and salt.

**6:3** And he offered upon the altar together with the salt, and he poured on it a fourth of a hin of oil.

**6:4** And Noah offered it as a sweet-savour, and it was acceptable before the LORD, and the LORD smelled the sweet savour.

**6:5** And the LORD said to him: "Build for yourself altars in all places where you see, and hallow them, and the sweet savour will be acceptable to me for all generations; for I have not yet created earth again."

**6:6** "But take heed that you eat no blood. For this reason I command you saying: 'You shall not eat any blood whatever, whether of beasts or fowl, or of any creature that moves on the earth, in the water, or in the air.'"

**6:7** "And if you do eat the blood, it will be for you a curse; and every one who eats the blood of any creature — the life thereof is in the blood — he shall die the death."

**6:8** "And every man who sheds man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed, for in the image of God made he man."

**6:9** "But you, increase and multiply on the earth."

**6:10** And Noah and his sons swore that they would not eat any blood that was in any flesh, and he made a covenant before the LORD God forever throughout all the generations of the earth in this month.

**6:11** On this account he spoke to you that you should make a covenant with the children of Israel in this month upon the mountain with an oath, and that you should sprinkle blood upon them because of all the words of the covenant, which the LORD made with them for ever.

**6:12** And this testimony is written concerning you that you should observe it continually, so that you should not eat on any day any blood of beasts or birds or cattle during all the days of the earth, and the man who eats the blood of beast or of fowl or of cattle during all the days of the earth, he and his seed shall be rooted out from under heaven.

**6:13** And do you command the children of Israel to eat no blood, so that their names and their seed may be before the LORD our God continually.

**6:14** And for this law there is no limit of days, for it is for ever. They shall observe it throughout their generations, so that they may continually make supplication on your behalf before the LORD our God with the blood they offer on the altar; and every day that you offer to him there will be pardon for us that we eat not the blood of the beast or the bird or the cattle.

**6:15** And behold I gave and ordained the commandment to the children of Noah, and to all flesh, not to cover the blood, but to pour it upon the earth and cover it with dust.

**6:16** And on this account I commanded the children of Israel: every man among them who hunts beast or fowl or that which lies in the water shall pour out its blood and cover it with earth.

**6:17** For the life is in the blood, and I commanded the children of Israel not to cover the blood, but to pour it upon the earth and cover it with dust; for this is the law and the ordinance which is commanded to the children of Israel.

**6:18** Behold this law has no limit of days, for it is forever; they shall observe it throughout their generations, so that they may make supplication on your behalf before the LORD our God with the blood they offer.

**6:19** And in this third month, in the first week of it, that is before Noah, this covenant was ordained, namely, that there should be a flood in the year when Noah died; for he had sworn by the throne of the LORD that he would not alter this covenant.

**6:20** And therefore on the new moon of the third month, he commanded them to fast and to afflict themselves, and that they should offer a burnt offering to the LORD; for this was the feast of Weeks and the feast of first-fruits; this feast was twofold and of a double nature: according to what is written and engraven concerning it on the heavenly tablets."

**6:21** For this reason it is ordained and written on the heavenly tablets that they should observe the feast of Weeks in this month once a year, to renew the covenant every year.

**6:22** And this whole festival was celebrated in heaven from the day of creation till the days of Noah — twenty-six jubilees and five weeks of years: and Noah and his sons observed it for seven jubilees and one week of years, till the day of Noah's death, and from the day of Noah's death his sons did away with it until the days of Abraham, and they ate blood.

**6:23** And Abraham alone kept it, and Isaac and Jacob and his children kept it up to your days, and in your days the children of Israel forgot it until ye celebrated it anew on this mountain.

**6:24** And do thou command the children of Israel to observe this festival in all their generations for a commandment unto them: one day in the year in this month they shall celebrate the feast, for it is the feast of Weeks and the feast of First Fruits.

**6:25** This whole festival was twofold and of a double kind: the first-fruits of the harvest and the renewal of the covenant was prescribed for it in all years, that Israel should remember and renew the covenant in this third month every year.

**6:26** And the whole number of the days of this year is three hundred and sixty-four days, divided into the weeks they are fifty-two weeks of days, and the remainder of the year, when its days have been reckoned, three hundred and sixty-four.

**6:27** And the command is ordained and graven on the heavenly tablets to keep the testimony of the years from this; and there is no neglecting (this commandment) for a single year or from year to year.

**6:28** And command thou the children of Israel that they observe the years according to this reckoning — three hundred and sixty-four days, and these will constitute a complete year, and they will not disturb its time from its days and from its feasts; for everything will fall out in them according to their testimony, and they will not leave out any day nor disturb any feasts.

**6:29** But if they do neglect and do not observe them according to his commandment, then they will disturb all their seasons and the years will be dislodged from this (order), and they will neglect their ordinances.

**6:30** And all the children of Israel will forget and will not find the path of the years, and will forget the new moons, and seasons, and sabbaths, and they will go wrong as to all the order of the years.

**6:31** For I know and from henceforth will I declare it unto thee, that the children of Israel will neglect this reckoning of the year, and will err in this intercalation, and they will adopt what has been prescribed for the Gentiles in this matter, and they will be astray as touching the new moons and times and sabbaths, and they will eat of all the blood with all flesh.

**6:32** And there will be people who will assuredly make observations of the moon — how (it) disturbs the seasons and comes before its time by two days: and these will reckon the years rightly without this reckoning.

**6:33** For I know they are contentious and will say: "the moon is the timepiece." And they will disturb and will lead astray those who do rightly, who will have their years reckoned, and they will be counted as exact by them.

**6:34** And all of them will call the seven weeks "Weeks of Years," that is, "Jubilees," seven times.

**6:35** And herewith is ended the account of the division of the days.

---
*EMET notes: The blood prohibition (vv.6-18) is Jubilees' key covenant-of-Noah law; it anchors the Noahic covenant as binding on all humanity, and specifically Israel via the Sinai renewal. The 364-day solar calendar (v.26) is a central Jubilees/Dead Sea Scrolls sectarian position against the lunar calendar (vv.32-33). "Feast of Weeks" = Shavuot; its institution attributed to Noah here.*
